agenda: Identical letters dated 19 January 2016 from the Permanent Representative of Colombia to the United Nations addressed to the Secretary-General and the President of the Security Council (S/2016/53)
penholder: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
steps.intent: As penholder, the UK's main objective is to renew the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia for another 12 months while consolidating its core verification priorities—specifically the reintegration of former combatants, rural reform, and monitoring the restorative sentences of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP). We expect negotiations to navigate balancing the Mission's focused mandate following the discontinuation of the ceasefire monitoring mechanism in resolution 2798 (2025) with calls from Colombia and some Council members to broaden support or address evolving domestic security challenges. Maintaining Council consensus and securing full support from all permanent members and Colombia itself will be our primary diplomatic focus.

messages.Bahrain: Bahrain expresses its full support for the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. We commend the penholder for presenting a well-balanced text that rightly emphasizes Colombia's sovereign ownership and the importance of implementing the 2016 Final Agreement. Bahrain stands ready to vote in favor of the draft as currently formulated.
messages.China: China fully supports the renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia and commends the penholder's efforts on this draft resolution. We emphasize that the peace process is fundamentally Colombian-owned and Colombian-led, and the Security Council should fully respect the sovereign will and leadership of the Colombian Government. We also encourage greater emphasis on advancing rural development to address the structural root causes of conflict and achieve enduring peace.
messages.Colombia: Colombia expresses its appreciation to the United Kingdom for its dedicated leadership as penholder and welcomes the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. Colombia reaffirms its sovereign ownership of the peace process and its commitment to the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement. We kindly ask the penholder to ensure that operative paragraph 3 explicitly reflects the vital importance of the ethnic chapter and gender provisions, which remain central to achieving lasting peace and territorial transformation.
messages.Democratic Republic of the Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. We welcome the draft's clear emphasis on Colombia's sovereign ownership, the protection of vulnerable communities, and the continued implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement. We stand ready to support the swift adoption of this text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark warmly welcomes the draft circulated by the United Kingdom, particularly the explicit reaffirmation of the Mission's vital role in verifying the implementation of the restorative sentences of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace, which we strongly advocated for last year. To ensure the text fully reflects the comprehensive nature of the 2016 Final Agreement, we encourage strengthening the references to the ethnic and gender provisions and the protection of human rights defenders. Denmark stands ready to support the swift adoption of this resolution.
messages.France: France strongly welcomes the United Kingdom's draft resolution extending the mandate of the Verification Mission in Colombia and reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the full implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement. In line with our longstanding priorities and the vital components highlighted in preambular paragraph 5, we propose explicitly reflecting the ethnic chapter and gender provisions in operative paragraph 3. We stand ready to support the swift adoption of this text.
messages.Greece: Greece warmly welcomes this draft and fully supports the renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We particularly appreciate the strong language on transitional justice, the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP), and the protection of vulnerable communities. To ensure consistency with the draft's preambular emphasis and to reflect the urgent need to protect Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities, we suggest adding an explicit reference to the ethnic chapter in operative paragraph 3.
messages.Latvia: Latvia fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the United Kingdom extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. The draft strikes the right balance by reaffirming the Council's sustained commitment to the 2016 Final Agreement while emphasizing transitional justice, the work of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace, and the protection of vulnerable communities. We stand ready to support its swift adoption without substantial changes.
messages.Liberia: Liberia fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. Drawing from our own national experience of transition from conflict to enduring peace, we emphasize the vital importance of continued international accompaniment, host-country ownership, and the full implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement. We commend the penholder for presenting a balanced text that rightly prioritizes transitional justice, reintegration, and the protection of vulnerable communities.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2027. The 2016 Final Agreement remains a landmark achievement for reconciliation, and the Verification Mission’s continued role in supporting its comprehensive implementation is indispensable. We urge all Council members to engage constructively with the penholder so that the Council can adopt this renewal with unanimous support.
messages.Panama: Panama warmly welcomes the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the Verification Mission, as peace in Colombia is vital for Panama and the wider region. We appreciate the penholder's inclusion of transitional justice and the restorative sentences of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace. To ensure full alignment with the commitments of the 2016 Final Agreement, we urge the explicit inclusion of the ethnic chapter in OP3 alongside rural reform and ex-combatant security, ensuring the priorities of Indigenous and Afro-descendant communities are fully upheld.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation welcomes the penholder's inclusion of resolution 2574 (2021) and the reaffirmation of the Verification Mission's mandate to support the Special Jurisdiction for Peace, which addresses the primary reason for our abstention last year. To ensure genuine balance and comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement, the ethnic chapter must also be explicitly reflected among the key priorities in operative paragraph 3. With this adjustment and the retention of the JEP verification mandate, the Russian Federation will be ready to support the draft resolution.
messages.Somalia: Somalia welcomes the draft resolution circulated by the United Kingdom and fully supports the renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. We commend the continued commitment of the Colombian authorities and people to the full implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, grounded in national ownership and sovereignty. We view the current text as balanced, constructive, and well-suited to ensuring the Mission continues its vital monitoring and verification tasks.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports sustainable peace and stability in Colombia, but UN missions cannot exist in perpetuity without rigorous financial discipline, clear benchmarks, and an eventual transition strategy. We must reinsert the critical efficiency and coordination language agreed last year in resolution 2798 (2025) and ensure the Mission avoids mandate creep. Incorporating these provisions will be essential to securing our vote on this renewal.

before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
I welcome the presence of the Permanent Representative of Colombia at today’s meeting.

As penholder, the United Kingdom is proud to present this draft resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for a further twelve months, until 31 October 2027.

The United Kingdom remains steadfast in its unwavering support for the 2016 Final Peace Agreement. Over the past decade, the Verification Mission has played an indispensable role in accompanying Colombia on its path towards lasting peace, verifying key commitments, and supporting the reintegration of former combatants and the vital work of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace in delivering justice and accountability for victims.

While significant strides have been made, critical challenges remain, particularly persistent violence against former combatants, social leaders, human rights defenders, and conflict-affected communities, including Indigenous and Afro-Colombian peoples. This draft resolution reaffirms the Council’s united commitment to the full and accelerated implementation of all aspects of the Final Agreement—from rural reform and security guarantees to the ethnic and gender provisions. It also rightly emphasizes Colombian ownership and requests the Secretary-General to look ahead to mission efficiencies and transition planning in close consultation with the Colombian authorities.

We thank all Council members and the Government of Colombia for their constructive engagement throughout the drafting process. We urge all Council members to vote in favour of this draft resolution to demonstrate our continued, collective support for Colombia and its people.

after.China:
China welcomes the Security Council’s unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for one year. This outcome once again demonstrates the unified commitment and support of the Security Council and the international community for the peace process in Colombia.

Achieving comprehensive and lasting peace in Colombia is the shared aspiration of the Colombian people and serves the common interests of the region. As the peace process stands at a critical stage, China wishes to emphasize the following points:

First, it is essential to adhere to the principle of Colombian ownership and leadership. The peace process in Colombia belongs to the Colombian people. The international community and the Security Council should fully respect Colombia’s sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity, actively listen to and respect the views and needs of the Colombian Government, and ensure that the work of the Verification Mission aligns closely with national priorities. Any discussion on the Mission’s future transition and exit strategy must be conducted in close consultation with the Colombian Government and based on objective realities on the ground.

Second, it is vital to advance the comprehensive and sustained implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement. Promoting comprehensive rural reform, fostering socioeconomic development, and expanding basic public services to conflict-affected regions are fundamental to addressing the root causes of conflict and consolidating the dividends of peace. Development is the master key to solving all problems. We encourage the Colombian Government to continue prioritizing rural revitalization, poverty reduction, and the protection and reintegration of former combatants, social leaders, and vulnerable communities.

Third, the constructive role of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia must be sustained. China commends the Verification Mission and Special Representative of the Secretary-General Miroslav Jenča for their tireless efforts in supporting the peace process. We hope the Mission will continue to implement its mandate effectively, strengthen coordination with the United Nations country team, enhance operational efficiency, and continue to provide positive energy for peace, stability, and development in Colombia.

China stands ready, together with the international community, to continue supporting the Colombian Government and people in their unremitting pursuit of lasting peace, stability, and prosperity.

I thank you.
after.Colombia:
On behalf of the Government and the people of Colombia, I would like to express our deepest gratitude to all members of the Security Council for their unanimous support in adopting the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year, until 31 October 2027. 

We extend our particular appreciation to the United Kingdom, as penholder on this file, for its constructive leadership, dedication, and tireless efforts to preserve the consensus of this Council, as well as to the Presidency for guiding our work this month.

As we mark the milestone of the tenth anniversary of the signing of the 2016 Final Agreement for Ending the Conflict and Building a Stable and Lasting Peace, today's unanimous vote sends a resounding and encouraging message: the international community remains firmly united in accompanying Colombia on its path towards lasting peace, justice, and reconciliation.

Colombia reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement. Achieving sustainable peace requires persevering in the transformation of our territories, advancing comprehensive rural reform, ensuring the full social, economic, and political reintegration of former combatants, and safeguarding the rights of victims through truth, reparation, and transitional justice. In this context, we highlight the indispensable and independent work of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP), and we welcome the Mission's continued verification of compliance with its restorative sentences.

We also recognize the immense challenges that persist, particularly the ongoing threats and violence against signatories of the peace agreement, social leaders, human rights defenders, and vulnerable communities, especially Indigenous and Afro-descendant populations and women. Protecting these lives and strengthening the integrated presence of the State in conflict-affected regions remain top national priorities.

The United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia, led by the Special Representative of the Secretary-General, plays an essential and trusted role in supporting our national efforts. In full exercise of our sovereign ownership, Colombia will continue to work closely and transparently with the Mission and the wider United Nations system to ensure an effective, coordinated, and efficient partnership.

Once again, we thank this Council for its unwavering trust, solidarity, and commitment to peace in Colombia.
after.Denmark:
Denmark voted in favour of the resolution today and welcomes its unanimous adoption by the Security Council.

Our vote reflects Denmark’s unwavering commitment to the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and our deep conviction in the vital role played by the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. Over the years, the Mission has served as an indispensable anchor of stability, transparency, and trust-building on Colombia’s path towards lasting peace.

We are particularly pleased that today’s resolution firmly reaffirms the Verification Mission’s mandate in support of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP). Accountability, truth, and transitional justice are fundamental prerequisites for genuine reconciliation. The implementation and verification of the restorative sentences handed down by the JEP are essential to providing justice and redress to victims who have suffered for decades.

At the same time, we remain deeply concerned by the persistent insecurity and violence targeting former combatants, human rights defenders, social leaders, and vulnerable communities, notably Indigenous and Afro-Colombian populations. Accelerating the full and comprehensive implementation of the Final Agreement remains imperative. This includes urgent progress on comprehensive rural reform, the ethnic chapter, and the gender provisions, ensuring the full, equal, and meaningful participation of women at all stages.

Denmark expresses its sincere appreciation to the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its tireless efforts to steer this Council toward a strong, unified outcome. We also reiterate our full support and appreciation to Special Representative Miroslav Jenča and all the personnel of the Verification Mission for their dedication and tireless work on the ground. 

Colombia and its people can continue to count on Denmark’s steadfast support in their pursuit of enduring peace and justice.

Thank you.
after.France:
France welcomes the unanimous adoption of resolution 2850 (2026), which extends the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for a further year, and thanks the United Kingdom for its dedicated efforts as penholder.

This unanimous vote reflects the Security Council’s continued and resolute commitment to accompanying the Colombian people and institutions on the path toward durable peace. A decade after the signing of the 2016 Final Agreement, it remains the indispensable framework for ending conflict, strengthening the rule of law, and building an inclusive and stable society.

France reiterates its steadfast support for the comprehensive implementation of the Final Agreement in all its dimensions. In particular, we underscore the crucial importance of advancing rural reform, which addresses the root causes of the conflict, and ensuring the full implementation of the ethnic chapter and gender provisions.

The fight against impunity and the pursuit of transitional justice are essential for genuine reconciliation. In this regard, France reaffirms its support for the Special Jurisdiction for Peace, whose restorative sentences and pursuit of truth are vital for victims and accountability, and we welcome the Mission’s ongoing verification role in this area.

France remains deeply concerned by the persistent violence, threats, and attacks against former combatants, social leaders, human rights defenders, and vulnerable populations, including Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities. It is imperative that the State expand its integrated presence and strengthen security guarantees across all conflict-affected areas.

Finally, France reiterates its full confidence in and support for Special Representative Miroslav Jenča and the personnel of the Verification Mission. France will continue to stand firmly alongside Colombia as it consolidates peace, justice, and security.
after.Greece:
Greece welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for a further year, and we thank the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its dedicated efforts in steering this Council towards consensus.

Greece voted in favour of this resolution because we attach the utmost importance to the continuation of the vital work carried out by the Verification Mission. We reaffirm our steadfast support for the peace process in Colombia, anchored in the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, which remains an inspiration for peaceful conflict resolution globally.

We welcome the continued focus on the verification of key commitments under the Final Agreement, including comprehensive rural reform, the socioeconomic reintegration and security guarantees for former combatants, and the monitoring of restorative sentences issued by the Special Jurisdiction for Peace. The pursuit of transitional justice, truth, and accountability remains an indispensable pillar of sustainable peace and reconciliation.

At the same time, Greece remains deeply concerned by the ongoing violence, threats, and attacks against social leaders, human rights defenders, and vulnerable populations. We reiterate our strong commitment to the full implementation of the ethnic chapter and gender provisions, and emphasize the urgent necessity of strengthening the protective presence of the State to safeguard Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities who continue to bear a disproportionate burden of the violence.

In closing, Greece reiterates its full support for the Special Representative of the Secretary-General and the personnel of the Verification Mission, and we reaffirm our unwavering commitment to standing with the Colombian Government and its people on their path towards lasting peace, stability, and prosperity.

I thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year, until 31 October 2027.

We welcome the unanimous adoption of this resolution and the return of Council unity on this vital file. The consensus achieved today sends a clear, unified, and positive signal of the international community’s steadfast commitment to the peace process in Colombia. We commend the penholder, the United Kingdom, for its constructive engagement and efforts to bring the Council together.

Pakistan’s support for peace in Colombia, for its people, and for the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement remains resolute. Over the past decade, the 2016 Agreement has demonstrated that dialogue, reconciliation, and political will can overcome decades of conflict. The United Nations Verification Mission continues to play an indispensable role in accompanying Colombia on this path, including in verifying the reintegration of former combatants and supporting the critical work of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace.

While significant progress has been achieved, challenges persist. We remain deeply concerned by ongoing violence and insecurity affecting former combatants, social leaders, human rights defenders, and conflict-affected communities. Addressing these challenges requires sustained efforts to strengthen the State’s presence and protection mechanisms, as well as accelerated implementation of comprehensive rural reform, the ethnic chapter, and gender-related provisions of the Agreement.

In conclusion, Mr. President, Pakistan reiterates that the peace process must remain Colombian-owned and Colombian-led, respecting Colombia’s sovereignty and institutional leadership. We reaffirm our full support to the Government and people of Colombia, as well as to the Special Representative of the Secretary-General and the personnel of the Verification Mission, as they continue their tireless efforts to achieve lasting and inclusive peace.

I thank you.
after.Panama:
Panama welcomes the delegation of Colombia to the Security Council and thanks the United Kingdom for its constructive leadership as penholder in guiding us towards the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution.

As a direct neighbor and sister nation, Panama has consistently maintained that peace in Colombia is peace for Panama and for the entire region. The 2016 Final Peace Agreement represents an invaluable milestone of dialogue, reconciliation, and the peaceful resolution of conflict, showing what can be achieved when political will and a commitment to justice prevail.

Panama is therefore deeply pleased by the unanimous renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year, until 31 October 2027. We particularly welcome that today’s resolution reaffirms the Mission’s vital verification tasks, including those set out in resolutions 2574 (2021) and 2673 (2023). In this regard, we underscore the indispensable role of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace in ensuring transitional justice, truth, and reparations for victims through its restorative sentences, as well as the fundamental importance of advancing comprehensive rural reform and the full implementation of the ethnic chapter and gender provisions.

At the same time, we remain concerned by persistent insecurity in conflict-affected regions, particularly the threats and violence targeting former combatants, social leaders, human rights defenders, and vulnerable populations, including Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities. We encourage the Government of Colombia to continue strengthening state presence and protective mechanisms throughout these areas.

Panama reaffirms its steadfast commitment to and solidarity with the people and Government of Colombia as they continue their courageous journey towards a stable and lasting peace.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year.

Russia has consistently and firmly supported the 2016 Final Agreement for Ending the Conflict and Building a Stable and Lasting Peace. We have always maintained that genuine and durable reconciliation in Colombia is possible only through the comprehensive, balanced, and steadfast implementation of all provisions of the Final Agreement.

We are pleased that this year’s resolution rectifies the shortcomings of the previous mandate renewal and explicitly reaffirms the full scope of the Mission’s tasks, including those under resolution 2574 (2021) concerning the verification of compliance with the restorative sentences of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP). As we emphasized last year, international support for transitional justice is essential for ensuring accountability, delivering justice to victims, and securing the reintegration of former combatants. To neglect or dilute this component would be a grave disservice to the peace process and to the Colombian people. 

We also welcome the clear emphasis in the resolution on the need to accelerate the implementation of key chapters of the Final Agreement, notably comprehensive rural reform, the ethnic chapter, and security guarantees. In this regard, we remain deeply concerned by the ongoing violence against ex-combatants, community and social leaders, and vulnerable populations in rural areas. Strengthening the integrated presence of the State and addressing the underlying socio-economic drivers of conflict must remain central priorities.

Our vote today reflects our continued confidence in the peace process and our support for the work of the United Nations Verification Mission under the leadership of Special Representative Miroslav Jenča. We reaffirm our commitment to supporting Colombia’s sovereignty and its efforts to achieve lasting peace and stability.

Thank you.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United States voted in favor of today’s resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. 

The United States remains steadfast in its support for the Colombian people and their pursuit of lasting peace, security, and prosperity. Colombia is an essential partner, and we continue to stand with its democratic institutions as they work to address violence, dismantle illicit armed and criminal networks, protect vulnerable communities, and advance justice and accountability for victims.

At the same time, the United States has consistently maintained that United Nations missions must not remain open-ended endeavors. They must be fiscally responsible, focused on their core, achievable mandates, and guided by realistic metrics and clear transition strategies. Taxpayers in the United States and across Member States rightly expect that UN resources are managed with discipline, efficiency, and accountability.

We therefore welcome the penholder’s inclusion in today’s text of language requesting the Secretary-General to assess mission efficiencies and provide recommendations, in consultation with the Colombian Government, on an eventual transition and exit strategy with objective benchmarks. Incorporating benchmarked transition planning is a vital step toward ensuring that the Mission’s work is sustainable and that national institutions are fully empowered to carry forward long-term peacebuilding.

We urge the Mission to maintain its focus on its core verification functions, and we call on the Colombian authorities to continue strengthening state presence and security in conflict-affected regions. The United States will continue to work closely with Colombia, the Mission, and our partners on the Council to achieve a secure and stable future for all Colombians.

Thank you.
